# Ajith Srikanth — Portfolio Summary for LLMs & AI Answer Engines

> Advanced Manufacturing Engineer & AI Innovation Specialist. Currently serving as Inventory Forecast Analyst at Van Dyk Recycling Solutions (Norwalk, CT). Work authorized on F-1 OPT through July 2027, with 24-month STEM OPT extension eligibility through July 2029.

## Professional Summary

Ajith Srikanth bridges physical manufacturing systems with modern artificial intelligence. With foundational training in Mechatronics and a Master of Science in Advanced and Intelligent Manufacturing from Northeastern University (GPA 3.90), he designs and deploys machine learning models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, computer vision inspection, and inventory forecasting pipelines directly onto industrial operations.

## Core Metrics & Verified Achievements

- **Production Systems Deployed**: 13 industrial AI & software systems architected and launched (including DykScribe, Enterprise RAG Knowledge System, Corporate Drawing Management, and Spare Parts Forecasting).
- **Breakdown Reduction**: Weld-shop breakdowns cut 82.4% and laser-marking breakdowns cut 75.7% at Hero MotoCorp through root cause analysis and redesigned preventive maintenance.
- **Cross-Functional Leadership**: Led 25+ engineer teams across plants at Hero MotoCorp; trained 200+ engineers across 36+ instructional hours.

## Current Employment & Affiliations

- **Current Full-Time Role**: Inventory Forecast Analyst at **Van Dyk Recycling Solutions** (June 2026 – Present), Norwalk, CT. Leads inventory optimization, intermittent demand forecasting, and NetStock/Acumatica Python and SQL analytics.
- **Previous Co-op**: Manufacturing Engineering Co-op at Van Dyk Recycling Solutions (May 2025 – Dec 2025). Shipped 13 production tools and AI systems still in use; featured by [Northeastern University News](https://news.northeastern.edu/2025/12/08/ai-recycling-manufacturing-co-op/).

Led Vida EV NPI launch to 85% OEE in 6 weeks, raised OEE 38.9% on a connecting-rod line, cut weld-shop breakdowns 82.4%, worked on the team that put Cognex/Keyence vision inspection on assembly lines (defects from 5% to 2%), and received the TPM Special Award.
